newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES END DOWN THE DAILY LIMIT.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO ALUMINIUM FUTURES END DOWN THE DAILY LIMIT.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures finished down by their daily limits across the board in very thin trade on Monday, hit by the dollar's sharp decline against the yen, traders said.
"The dollar's fall bit the most today," said one trader. "But there's not change in the (bullish) sentiment. Only people are watching the precious metals market."
By the close in Tokyo, the dollar was trading just above 115 yen, compared with above 118 yen on Friday.
Most of the aluminium futures here were glued to their limit-downs for the whole day, with the June finishing down six yen at 197.8 yen per kilo. Estimated volume was 1,583 lots.
In Tokyo precious metals market, where platinum group metals (PGMs) have seen large swings lately, most contracts dropped except for palladium futures, which climbed on short-covering.
On Friday in London, the benchmark three-month aluminium finished down $16.5 at $1,746 per tonne as it found renewed buying interest after correcting lower to touch $1,732.
